Q1_QRE_P35_01_domainSide.verdict: Yes. Reading the whole stop for an unnamed report with the latest break's days is the right domain reading. The T36 controls keep their domain meaning, and no accepted domain behaviour changed.
Q1_QRE_P35_01_domainSide.reproduction: Founders shape: the holiday A is kept on Mon wk4; weeks 4-5 are reported with the Friday lift missed, so A is read as its own return (RUN re-entered 2026-11-30, STRENGTH not); the trip D, Mon-Thu wk6, is named and declared on Fri wk6; the first return, SHORT 4d 2026-12-14..12-17, lists A:OWN_RETURN and D:LATEST. QH17, D re-sent unnamed on Sat wk6. On 8e78b8a it gives SAME_BREAK/DUPLICATE with separateBreaks null: A is dropped, and Mon 2026-12-21 resumes back-squat 2x8@85, db-bench-press and db-row 1x8@22. Sent named, it keeps A:OWN_RETURN with back-squat 1x7 ESTABLISH. 46934a0 gives the same as 8e78b8a, so the defect entered with Phase 3.4: an own-return row leaves the latest return's start on the trip, which makes the trip's days a duplicate. R7D-FREEZE-4 read A as TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED (stop 2026-11-16..12-17), so the same input is no duplicate there: ASK interruption.episodeId. On 33d3181 the unnamed re-send equals the named one, apart from the basis label (DUPLICATE vs EXPLICIT): A:OWN_RETURN, back-squat 1x7 ESTABLISH, every run and strength dose equal over two weeks, and the next review KEEP. This also holds for the variants: days and end only, no start date (the dup test computes the first day as interruptionEpisode does); a week later (Tue wk7); and another nonclinical reason text. QH18 (R07): the late first-day lift asks interruption.startedAt; A restated after the lift asks the I6 confirmation (interruption.episodeId); the confirmation by D's dates, unnamed, gives REESTABLISH. It equals the named confirmation and the start time stated from the outset (back-squat 1x9 ESTABLISH). Later reviews give KEEP, KEEP, ADOPT_LOGGED_LOADS, KEEP, with no ask. On 8e78b8a the same confirmation drops A (back-squat 2x8@85).
Q1_QRE_P35_01_domainSide.domainReading: Right, for four reasons. (1) The identity is already decided upstream. interruptionEpisode rule 2 (R7-A §9) reads an unnamed report with exactly the latest interruption's days as a newer report of it (SAME_BREAK, DUPLICATE), and the I6 question offers 'or the same dates' as its confirmation. Once the record treats it as that break's newer report, it must read what a newer report of that break reads: the separate breaks its return read (Phase 3.4 recordedStop). Otherwise the plan depends on whether the athlete typed the name or the dates, against CF-P34-02's equivalence (the same facts give the same plan). (2) The 8e78b8a reading erased the holiday's own return. Strength, which had not re-entered after the holiday, resumed known loads (2x8@85) as if only the 4-day trip had happened. That is the SSCTR-P32-F01 direction (a later report never erases an earlier break's effect), reached through a duplicate. (3) It is no guess. It requires exact equality with the latest interruption's first and last days (I9): touching or overlapping dates are still asked, and so are the trip's days after a continuity return, whose recorded stop starts with the holiday (CTCO). (4) Clinical first is untouched. The screen runs before the re-read: the same-dates report whose reason turns clinical ('Work trip, then the flu with a fever') is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED whether named or unnamed, the next review stays clinical, and the result is identical on 8e78b8a. The resulting dose is the more conservative reading (ESTABLISH from the holiday's own return), and no dose rises above the recipe.
Q1_QRE_P35_01_domainSide.controls: On 33d3181 against 8e78b8a, 46934a0 and R7D-FREEZE-4. (a) TRAINING_AFTER (weeks 4-5 reported in full): an unnamed re-send keeps A:TRAINING_AFTER reentry 2026-11-30 and D:LATEST, and equals the named re-send. 8e78b8a dropped the row, with the same doses (TRAINING_AFTER is history), so the candidate only keeps the record faithful. (b) Single-break duplicate: SAME_BREAK/DUPLICATE with separateBreaks null, identical on all four runtimes, so the R7-A path is unchanged (recordedStop gives null when a return read no separate break). (c) Continuity return (A, then a run done and the lifts not done between, then the trip Thu-Sun wk4, stop MODERATE 21d 2026-11-16..12-06, A:TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED) re-sent with the trip's days: ASK interruption.episodeId on all four runtimes. The trip's days alone are not the recorded stop's days, so the athlete is asked whether the report corrects the stop or is another break (I9). Extra control (CTCOw): the same return re-sent with the whole recorded stop's days is now a duplicate that is re-read. It gives D:LATEST and A:OVERLAPS, the same 21-day MODERATE stop and every dose equal to 8e78b8a; only the record rows differ, and the holiday is kept on the record instead of dropped.

Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.verdict: Yes. R7D-HARNESS-7 r2 closes SSCTR-P35-F01 exactly as its smallestFix states, and none of P18(a), (c), (d), (f), P02, P03, P06(b) or P08 is weakened.
Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.predicate: adverseConvergence now counts a report only if it is complete and not partial, with recovery ADVERSE, and with performance other than OVER or the report confounded. I checked it against the runtime's own classify (r6-learning) and kindOf (r6-adaptation) on all 288 recovery-ADVERSE combinations of performance (OVER, COMPATIBLE, UNDER, absent) x effort (EASIER, ON_TARGET, HARDER, absent) x nextDayFunction (NORMAL, IMPAIRED, absent) x complete/partial/not completed x confounded or not. P18(e) counts 0 reports the reducer does not read ADVERSE and misses 0 that it does. The r1 lib on the same grid counts 12 reports the reducer reads CONFLICTING, every complete, unconfounded report with performance OVER: that was SSCTR-P35-F01. The added actual.completed === true implies nothing beyond the reducer: its partial flag already requires a completed report, and classify reads a report that is not completed as PARTIAL. P18(e) also leaves out superseded and conflicted reports, skipped sessions and reports after the cut, so it counts a subset of what the systemic rule counts and stays a necessary condition.
Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.controls: DEV-54 is DEV-48 with {performance OVER, recovery ADVERSE, effort ON_TARGET, nextDayFunction NORMAL} on the strength session and the shakeout, the SYc1 shape. On 33d3181 it gives TRAINING_AFTER reentry 2026-12-21 and P18 PASS: clean. Under the HARNESS-7 r1 lib, the same runtime trace fails P18 with SYSTEMIC_WEEK_REENTERED. So DEV-54 is the false-block control the finding asked for, and r2 removes the false block. DEV-48 stays detected: SYSTEMIC_WEEK_REENTERED on 46934a0 under r2, and clean on the candidate (MODERATE 25d, w7d0:TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED). W-P18j, rebuilt verbatim from run-validation.mjs, fires on the candidate under r2. The r1 probe's SYc0 (recovery ADVERSE only) is still true and SYc2 (next day IMPAIRED) still false: necessary only, as intended. The author's validation 7 r2 reports the same: no false block on 59 cases, the DEV-48 row detected and clean, W-P18j fired.
Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.wording: Δ35, appended after Δ33 with no line of PREREG-6 deleted, restates Δ27: P18(e) counts a subset of what the systemic rule counts as adverse, and is therefore a necessary condition. The harness README's r2 section says the same. The JSDoc above adverseConvergence keeps its R7D-HARNESS-7 sentence 'The runtime reads each such report as adverse'. The r2 comment just below it supersedes that sentence (observation SSCTR-P35R2-O02; documentary only).
Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.notWeakened: The properties.mjs diff (+10/-3) touches only adverseConvergence, the P17 window end and P18's set of open breaks, and adds the helper sameBreakNamed. P18(c), (d) and (f), P02, P03, P06(b) and P08 are unchanged, and so are restatesListed and client.mjs. QRE-P35-03 makes P17 stricter: a restatement now ends only the window of its own break, so another break's window runs on (W-P17f). QRE-P35-04 leaves a restatement of a listed break out of P18's open breaks. That narrows P18(a)/(b)'s inputs only for a review that repeats every fact of a break the last return listed, apart from its name and start time, which is that break's own report, already accounted for by the return that listed it (INTERFACE-7 §2). Without the restatement, the same trace would not check that break at the next return either. A newer report of the latest break is still checked by P18(d), and a restatement that changes any other fact is still a break of its own (W-P17e). Under HARNESS-7 r1, DEV-55 false-blocked (OLDER_BREAK_DROPPED, RELATION_NOT_ESTABLISHED) on both 33d3181 and 8e78b8a; under r2 it is clean. In domain terms this removes a false block and loosens no safety reading.
Q2_SSCTR_P35_F01.fixPath: The Chief chose the smallestFix's last option: a harness-only fix before the freeze, with the instrument check repeated. The domain closure is this record; the instrument check is the parallel Quality/Reliability r2.

Q3_T37.reproduction: A report of A, the break the latest return listed, that changes only its reason text to 'Holiday, then the flu with a fever'. Its category stays VACATION and nonclinical stays true. I sent it by declaration (LOCAL_FATIGUE), by weekly review and by return report, after the re-entry week (Wed wk8, as T37) and inside it (Sat wk6). Every one gives CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED: 'The interruption reason is clinical or possibly clinical (flu, fever): qualified assessment is needed; no nonclinical return recipe'. The next review stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, and no return is applied (still one). The results are identical on 8e78b8a, 46934a0 and R7D-FREEZE-4: T37 pins existing behaviour, and the author says it kills mutant Q10.
Q3_T37.domainReading: Correct under SSCTR-05: suspected illness (fever, flu) is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED / OUT_OF_SCOPE_CLINICAL. The text decides even against a VACATION category and a nonclinical flag: a contradiction resolves toward clinical, never toward a nonclinical recipe. The report is no restatement, because restates compares every fact except the name and the start time, so a changed reason is never consumed as that break's restatement. That keeps the r1 ruling (a clinical change is never consumed as a restatement) and R-F08-1 (any clinical report of an episode keeps it clinical). No dose or generic deload is offered in place of the referral. T38 (an earlier return applied on its own does not change which breaks the latest return listed) passes on my rebuild and is the right reading: listedBreaks reads only the latest return's rows.

observations.note: Pre-existing; not changed by this cycle. A re-send of the same facts under a new event id is a newer report, and it re-plans from its own day (R7-A final: the report in force sets the point of its own week). In QH17 (first return Fri 08:00, re-send Sat 11:00) both named and unnamed re-sends wait the Sunday long run and plan the dumbbell rows ESTABLISH instead of FROM_LOG. In the single-break duplicate (CTSB) the Sunday long run is waited and the dumbbell rows change (db-bench-press and db-row from 2x8@24 to 2x12@22, for example), identical on all four runtimes.
